questions_and_answers.answer: What are "asset-price bubbles" as described/illustrated in the textbook, and what is the general cause of an asset-price bubble (provide some examples)? A). "Asset-price bubbles" occur when asset prices in wholesale markets (i.e., steel, aluminum, or labor) are driven well-above the assets' fundamental economic values by management psychology B). "Asset-price bubbles" occur when asset prices in consumer markets (i.e., autos, food, or or gasoline) are driven well-above the assets' fundamental economic values by consumer psychology. C). "Asset-price bubbles" occur when asset prices in specific assets markets (i.e., the stock market or real estate market) are driven well-above the assets' fundamental economic values by investor psychology.
